Content:
Let's look at the following right triangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/770b5cc7e4cb05d7adb9af31ca46ee3d]

Content:
How can we find its area?

Content:
It turns out that:

Content:
> The area of a right triangle is half the area of the corresponding rectangle:
> [MATH: \text{Area of Triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \text{(Area of Rectangle)}.]

Content:
In our case, the corresponding rectangle has dimensions [MATH: 8\:\text{m}] by [MATH: 6\:\text{m}.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/aa33a5d61f1c0e2955f6c2099a8fa035]

Content:
The area of the rectangle is
[MATH: Area of Rectangle|= 8m ⋅ 6m; = (8 ⋅ 6)(m ⋅ m); = 48m^{2}.]

Content:
Therefore, the area of the triangle is
[MATH: \textrm{Area of Triangle}
= \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 48
= 24 \: \text{m}^2.]

Content:

[MATH: Area of Triangle = (1)/(2) ⋅ 70 = 35ft^{2}.]
